# 08-fresco — sources

Back-test entry `08-fresco.yaml`: Fresco, the AI scribe for construction superintendents (YC Fall 2024).
Written 2026-10-22 from public material only. Quotes are verbatim from the page named; "Author's choice" marks the
smallest plausible choice made where the public material is silent.

Main sources:
- [HN] Launch HN: Fresco (YC F24), 2024-11-21 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42204939
- [LYC] Launch YC: Fresco, the scribe for construction, 2024-10-23 — https://www.ycombinator.com/launches/M73-fresco-the-scribe-for-construction
- [YCP] YC company page — https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/fresco (now "AI-powered takeoff and estimating for Division 8 construction")
- [KOE] A contractor's daily-log expectations on Procore's support site — https://support.procore.com/tc/Koester/Site_Map/Koester_Expectations_-_Daily_Logs
- [SWI] Swiftask, Procore daily reports page (vendor) — https://swiftask.ai/ai-integration/procore/intelligent-daily-reports
- [BLS] BLS Occupational Outlook, construction managers — https://www.bls.gov/ooh/management/construction-managers.htm
- [OPU] Launch HN: Opusense (field reports for site inspectors), 2025-05-20 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44042791

## The eight founder-emulation items

1. **Who.** Construction superintendents on commercial jobs.
   [HN] "Superintendents are the busiest and most expensive people on construction sites."
   [LYC] "That’s the reality for 210k+ construction superintendents (or supervisors, foremen, PMs, etc.) across the USA."
   → `roles[superintendent]`, `context.actor`, `actor_plural`. Author's choice: "on commercial jobs" (the founders ask
   for introductions to commercial general contractors in [LYC]).

2. **What (the job).** Keep the record of the day's work, for liability and disputes.
   [HN] "30-200 photos per day to document site progress (mostly for liability reasons, or in case of a dispute with the
   owner over delays and deliverables)"; photos used to create "daily logs", "structured documents that account for the
   work done on site on any given day". [KOE] the log is "a critical piece of documentation in the arbitration of a
   dispute". → `statements.problem`, `context.job`, `interpretations.problem`.

3. **When / where.** At the end of the day, after the site walks, in the trailer.
   [HN] "At the end of the day, they'll spend a few hours uploading those photos into OneDrive, or project management
   software like Procore or ACC." [YCP] "We were curious what superintendents were doing for hours in their trailers at
   the end of the day." [LYC] "supes are spending up to 3 hours a day creating documents". → `context.circumstance`, `occasion: daily log`.
   Author's choice: the recall window {5, WORKING_DAYS} and Frequency 4 to 5 working days out of 5 (the posts say "per
   day"; a five-day site week is assumed). Prevalence `p_80_100` ("Nearly all") follows from the same "per day".

4. **Which people (the comparable group).** Superintendents at US general contractors whose jobs run on Procore or ACC.
   [LYC] "210k+ construction superintendents ... across the USA"; "Project management tools like Procore and ACC have
   dramatically increased documentation requirements". [YCP] "driving to Napa, South Bay, and around SF". → `context.segment`,
   `market: US`.

5. **Who pays.** The general contractor, per site.
   [HN] "we charge per site per month, which includes unlimited users on any given construction project".
   → `persona.decision_maker: {role: contractor}`, the BUYER role. Author's choice: the decider is the contractor's
   "operations lead" and the role to test is "The CFO" (a second role, "The project executive", listed); Purchase
   friction's three steps ("A trial on one live job" tested, a Procore check, a security review) and Commitment's step
   "start a paid pilot on one site" are the author's. Public material names no buyer title; [LYC] asks for
   introductions to general contractors by firm, not by role.

6. **Mechanism.** Narrated short videos turned into notes, texted to the crew, pushed to Procore/ACC.
   [HN] "Supers simply take short videos with voiceover, or upload photos, and Fresco does the rest, creating notes with
   transcription, photos, assignees, and due dates. Supers can easily text their crew action items, and receive texts
   back". "We also route this to whatever project management software they're using with a single click."
   [LYC] the narrated example "The beam in the southwest corner of room 134 is corroded and needs replacement by Alex.";
   "Supes who use Fresco complete their notes, on average, 90% faster."
   → `statements.solution`, `solution_mechanism`, Compatibility and Adoption friction items. Relative advantage's two
   benefits are from [HN] ("during their site walks, not after") and [LYC] ("90% faster"); their wording is the author's.

7. **Price.** About $1k per site per month, less with multi-site or multi-month terms.
   [HN] "The typical price is $1k/month, but we offer discounts for multi-month or multi-site commitments."
   → `commercial.price` {800, 1000, month}. Author's choice: the low end of $800 stands for the stated discounts.
   Existing sacrifice: 30 to 60 hours a month per site at an hourly rate of 55 — from [LYC] "up to 3 hours a day" and
   [HN] "a few hours uploading", taken as 1.5 to 3 hours on about twenty working days (author's arithmetic). The rate is
   [BLS] "$55.28 per hour" (median, construction managers, May 2025), the author's stand-in: no superintendent wage is
   in the public material. Ability to pay is derived by code (24% to 61%).

8. **Occasions.** The narrated beam; a school refit report; the uploads and logs at the end of the day.
   [LYC] on a school refit walkthrough: "Normally, creating the final report takes 2+ hours."
   [HN] "few supers have time to do this thoroughly, so these photos aren't very searchable." No named customer quote
   exists in public; the occasions below are scripted from these and from practitioner comments.

No respondent carries the name of a commenter, customer or founder.

## Open
- The verdict was scripted to be plausible and not obviously "build": the problem holds on how often but people
  disagree on whether the log is one of their two worst difficulties; the solution splits on the benefit and on
  talking over videos on site; the price fails (two of eight at the founder's band or above) while the cost it would
  replace is above the price. This is the author's reading of the thread's sceptics, not a measured result.
- No public account names a buyer title at a general contractor; the decider, the tested role "The CFO", the purchase
  steps and the Commitment step are the author's.
- hourly_rate 55 is a proxy (construction managers, not superintendents).
- Existing sacrifice picks use `period: quarter` (the corpus's convention), although the registry's recall period for a
  monthly cost reads "last month"; the values are the monthly figures times three.
- The window {5, WORKING_DAYS} is the author's; the public posts say "per day".

screens.why4: The three steps are distinct and in my words, but the upload-photos route is missing, and nothing shows why the belief covers only the first row.
screens.why5: This keeps my narrated-video mechanism, but it drifts a little by dropping "or upload photos", so the belief tests talking over videos as the only way in.
screens.instead: Keep the belief, and change the first row to: Take short videos and talk over them on site walks, or upload your photos.

screens.why1: Right after I said what they would have to do to start, it makes sense to ask which of those steps is the one to test, and it closes the solution step as 4 of 4.
screens.why2: Short videos, talking over them, walks, notes, and Procore or ACC are all how I and my supers already talk, so I get it on first read.
screens.why3: I have spent months watching supers walk sites and know that talking over videos in the field is the behavior my product depends on, so I can pick the riskiest step from what I know.
screens.why4: The three options are distinct and cover the real steps of capture, review and connection, in my words, and no escape chip is needed because I am choosing among my own beliefs.
screens.why5: It keeps my mechanism of short videos with voiceover and routing to Procore or ACC, and the belief and the 1-in-3 bar state plainly what I picked to test.

screens.why1: Just before the study goes out is the obvious time to decide whether to ask people for a real pilot, and nothing earlier asked this.
screens.why2: Pilot is an everyday word to me, but "people who say yes" takes a second read because it doesn't say what they said yes to, and I haven't seen the Pilot tab yet.
screens.why3: Whether I want pilot leads from this study is my own call, since getting a live job signed up is what I'm chasing.
screens.why4: Yes or no covers the choice, the two options are distinct, and the wording is plain.
screens.why5: My pilot is a paid one on one site that the contractor agrees to, but "try this for real, leave your email" is a softer ask that doesn't mention payment, a site or who can approve it.
screens.instead: Offer a pilot? At the end, anyone who is interested sees: "Would you try this for real on one of your jobs? Leave your email." You'll see their emails on the Pilot tab. Options: Yes, ask them / No pilot

screens.why1: Just before the study goes out, choosing who will do the asking on the AI link is an obvious last setup step and has not been asked before.
screens.why2: The question is clear, but the hint packs in several points and 'the other face' and 'credits' take a second read for a founder who has seen no faces explained yet in the flow.
screens.why3: Which interviewer my superintendents would hear is my call to make, and I can decide it by listening to the voice.
screens.why4: The two names are distinct and enough for a preselected pick, but bare first names say nothing about the voice or how each would sound to a super unless the face and audio are shown.
screens.why5: It keeps my segment as I typed it, superintendents at US general contractors, and my preselected pick stands as Daphne.
screens.instead: Who should ask superintendents at US general contractors your questions? Daphne is already picked; tap Saskia to hear her instead. Recording the voice you choose uses 400 credits, and people get the link by text either way.

screens.why1: Just before the study goes out, it makes sense to choose how my superintendents will answer, though the 'SENT' kicker reads oddly because nothing has been sent yet.
screens.why2: The question is plain, but 'Every answer in a quiet room. More than 9 in 10 where it is loud' never says it means answers being captured correctly, so I had to read it twice, and I'd say 'jobsite', not 'building site'.
screens.why3: I know my supers are on loud jobsites and in trailers with a phone in hand, so I can judge whether they would talk, type or tap.
screens.why4: The three choices are complete and distinct, but a stray 'recording' dangles at the end of 'Let them choose' and the Daphne option's 'Hear it recording' reads like leftover button text.
screens.why5: It doesn't change or misstate anything I typed about Fresco, and my pick of 'Text only' is shown as one of the choices.
screens.instead: How should they answer? — AI interviewer, Daphne: she asks each question aloud on video, and they talk, type or tap (she catches every answer in a quiet room and more than 9 in 10 on a loud jobsite) / Text only: they read each question and tap or type / Let them choose: they pick Daphne or text when they open the link.

screens.why1: Right after choosing how they answer, the last step before sending is who receives the link, so it is obvious why this is asked here.
screens.why2: The three choices read plainly on first pass; 'the Contacts page' is the only Keel-specific term and its meaning is clear from 'a search'.
screens.why3: I know whether I have supers' names from our site visits and GC intros or would need a list or a post in a group, so I can answer from what I actually do.
screens.why4: The options are distinct and cover names, a found list and an open link, but 'a group' needs a shared place supers already gather, and the Google sign-in could put off supers who use a work account or just their phone, a catch that sits on only this one option.
screens.why5: My pick of 'People I know by name' is kept as typed, and nothing here changes what I said about my product or roles.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' is stated at the top, and each card ties it to the deciding number: 4 answered, 5 needed.
screens.why_b2: This page draws no chart, and although the 4-against-5 count is plain, I need a second look to see why 7 answered became 4 counted, and my 1-in-3 bar isn't shown.
screens.why_b3: The three dimension names and belief lines are the ones I checked on the way in, word for word.
screens.why_b4: '5 needed' implies I need at least one more anchored answer per belief, but the screen doesn't say that or what it means for building Fresco.
screens.why_b5: It rightly refuses to call the result on low n, but '7 people answered' sits unexplained above the 4 counted, and '0 of 3 holding' could read as failing rather than undecided.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 7 answered, but only 4 could be counted on each belief and 5 are needed, so this neither supports nor sinks the solution yet; get at least one more superintendent who walked a site in the last 5 working days before deciding what to build.

screens.why_b1: "Too few to call" is stated plainly, and right under it "4 answered · 5 needed to call it" gives the number that decides it.
screens.why_b2: The four answers and their counts read at once, but no bar is drawn or stated, because "You said they could talk over the noise on site" only repeats my belief and never says how many yeses it would need.
screens.why_b3: The name Compatibility and the belief line are word for word what I checked on the way in.
screens.why_b4: It tells me I'm one short of five but not what to do: nothing about getting one more answer, what that answer could change, or what this means for relying on narrated videos on site.
screens.why_b5: It rightly makes no call on 4 people and shows the guess as not counted, but Tomasz reads "Yes, with some steps" where the bar says "Yes, mostly", and the crane quote filed under Compatibility is about the log waiting, not about noise.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 3 of the 4 counted said they could talk over the noise and 1 said no, but it takes 5 answers and at least X yeses to call it, so get one more superintendent's answer from a live site before you bet on narrated video; Ray's no is the one to chase.

screens.why_b1: "Too few to call" sits directly above the number that decides it, 4 answered with 5 needed, though "4 answered" above five names takes a moment until I see Luis was not counted.
screens.why_b2: What is counted and over how many are plain (Better 3, Same 1, 1 of 4), but the bar line only repeats "hours back at the end of the day" and never shows the limit of no more than 1 in 3, so I have to remember it from the way in.
screens.why_b3: The name and belief line are exactly what I checked, including "hours back at the end of the day".
screens.why_b4: It never says what this means for the idea or what to do next, so I have to infer from "5 needed" that I need one more usable answer from a superintendent.
screens.why_b5: It makes no claim from these few answers: n stays visible, the low count is said outright, the guess is left out of the count, and Denise's dissent is shown.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 4 usable answers and 5 needed, because Luis's was a guess; 1 of 4 said no difference and the belief holds only if no more than 1 in 3 do, so get one more superintendent's answer about a specific log before deciding on the hours-back pitch.

screens.why_b1: "Too few to call" is the plain answer, and "4 answered · 5 needed to call it" sits right under it and explains why.
screens.why_b2: I can see four people counted across the four answers, but no bar is marked ("You said take short videos and talk over them on walks" gives no threshold), and I have to work out which bars would count toward "most".
screens.why_b3: The title and the line "Most would take short videos and talk over them on walks" are exactly the belief I checked on the way in.
screens.why_b4: "5 needed" implies I need one more answer, but nothing says so or tells me what this leaning result means for the video-on-walks idea.
screens.why_b5: The count is honest and the low n is stated, but the chart says "Only if I'd seen it work on one walk first" while Tomasz and Ray read "Yes, if it was clearly worth it · shown apart", so a softer or different condition looks like one settled answer that is both charted and set apart.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 4 counted and 5 needed, and only 1 of the 4 is a plain yes, 2 would do it only with a condition and 1 probably wouldn't; get one more superintendent's answer, and meanwhile show a skeptical super it working on one real walk, because that's the condition to test.

screens.why_b1: Each box says "Too few to call", but the deciding number (4 answered, 5 needed) is not on this screen, and the group counts of 1 and 2 don't explain the call.
screens.why_b3: Compatibility, Relative advantage and Adoption friction are the names I checked, but my belief lines are missing, so I have to map headings like "What gets in the way" back to talking over site noise or getting hours back.
screens.why_b4: Nothing says to get at least one more answer or what these quotes mean for the idea, so I'm left to work out the next step myself.
screens.why_b5: "Too few to call" is honest and nothing claims more than these people said, but the total of 4 isn't shown, and the same two people recur across boxes, which can read like more voices than there are.
screens.why_b6: I didn't type that the schedule and no-show subs outrank the log, that the log can wait till morning, or that one super would need to see it work on one walk first, though this comes from only two people.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 4 of the 5 answers needed, and only 2 explained why. Both say the schedule and subs press harder than the log, and one would need to see it work on a walk first, so get more answers and offer a one-walk demo before trusting this.

screens.why1: It's the first screen and an obvious check on whether I'm the right person, since a study about site paperwork needs to know what platform my jobs are on.
screens.why2: Procore and ACC are names I use every day, so I can answer the moment I hear it, even if 'run on' is a little loose.
screens.why3: I know exactly what software my current jobs use, because I'm the one putting logs and photos into it.
screens.why4: Yes and No are clean and a gate needs no escape chip, but a super with one job on Procore and another on something else has no clear answer.
screens.why5: It keeps the Procore-or-ACC segment and leaks no product or plan, just a plain check on what my jobs run on.
screens.why6: It's short and easy to answer by ear, but 'I'll read 2 options' is stiff before a plain yes or no, and 'ACC' only works because I already know it.
screens.instead: Is at least one job you're running now on Procore or ACC? Yes; or No.

screens.why1: After checking I'm on Procore or ACC, it makes sense to ask whether I actually did this log work in the past week, and it leads straight into the story about my last log.
screens.why2: Walk notes, re-type and daily log are how I'd talk about this, and I get it on the first read.
screens.why3: I do the daily log myself, so I know whether I typed up my walk notes this past week.
screens.why4: Yes and No cover it, but "I can't recall one particular daily log" is odd because the question isn't about one log, and two escape chips is one too many.
screens.why5: Nothing about a product reaches me, but "re-type your walk notes" narrows the job of getting the day's photos and notes into the log and leaves the photos out.
screens.why6: Said aloud it is one short question ending in "Yes or no", and I can answer it after hearing it once.
screens.instead: In the last 5 working days, did you put your site walk photos or notes into the daily log after the walk? Yes / No

screens.why1: After asking how I get my walk notes into the daily log, showing me an idea for that same chore is an obvious next step, and the part label tells me it's coming.
screens.why2: Site walk, assignees, due dates, action items, Procore and ACC are all everyday words on my job, and "AI scribe" is clear enough from the sentence around it.
screens.why3: I walk the site, take photos, hand out items to the crew and work in Procore, so I can picture this on my own job.
screens.why4: This is a card to read, with no options, chips or box to answer in.
screens.why5: The idea comes through clearly and shown on purpose, but the "people building it believe" line just repeats the description instead of saying what they believe it would do for me, and "the AI scribe" sounds like their product talk rather than how anyone on site would say it.
screens.why6: The short sentences say well, but the last one is a long mouthful that repeats everything I just heard, so by then I've stopped listening.
screens.instead: Imagine Fresco. During the site walk, you take short videos and talk over them. The AI turns them into notes with photos, assignees and due dates, texts the crew their action items, and sends the notes to Procore or ACC in one click. The people building it believe it would save you re-typing your walk notes into the daily log.

screens.why1: After the idea card, asking about talking on site makes some sense if the idea is voice notes, but it arrives abruptly because nothing here says why my talking matters.
screens.why2: The words are simple, but 'talk over the noise' needs a second read: does it mean talking to a crew member, or into a phone, and the daily log itself is something I do at the trailer, not over noise.
screens.why3: I know how loud my sites get, but the log is usually written in the trailer after the walks, so I would have to guess that it means dictating during the walk.
screens.why4: The scale covers the range and the escape fits, but 'Yes, easily' and 'Yes, mostly' sit close together, and 'mostly' is hard to separate from 'Only sometimes'.
screens.why5: Nothing of the founder's plan leaks beyond the name on the card, but 'Imagine Fresco' tells me nothing on its own, and the question seems to have drifted from whether voice capture fits my walk into a loose question about noise.
screens.why6: It is two short sentences with four short options and one escape, easy to hear once and hold.
screens.instead: Think of your last site walk. Could you have spoken your notes into your phone over the noise? Yes, easily; Yes, mostly; Only sometimes; or No. Or say I can't tell.

screens.why1: Right after the idea card and the question about talking over site noise, it makes sense to ask whether this thing would have helped on my last log.
screens.why2: It's short and easy to follow, but "go better" is vague for a daily log, because I'd have to decide whether that means faster, more accurate or easier to back up in a delay dispute.
screens.why3: I know exactly how my last log went, but I've never used Fresco, so whether it would have helped is partly a guess from the card.
screens.why4: The options run cleanly from a lot better to worse, they don't overlap, and "I can't tell" fits for someone who has only read a card.
screens.why5: The idea is named on purpose under the card and nothing else about the product or the founder's terms comes through; it only asks whether it would have helped.
screens.why6: It's one short question with four short options that I can hold after hearing them once, and the escape comes last.
screens.instead: Would Fresco have made your last daily log quicker to finish, or not? A lot quicker; a little quicker; no difference; or slower. Or say I can't tell.

screens.why1: After asking whether I could talk over the noise and whether it would have helped my log, it makes sense to ask if I'd actually do what the thing needs from me.
screens.why2: Short videos, talking over them, walks: that's how I'd say it, and I get it on the first read.
screens.why3: I walk the job and take photos every day, so I know whether I'd shoot video and talk on those walks.
screens.why4: The four cover it and I can't-tell fits, but 'Probably not' and 'No' sit close together, the conditional answer is a different kind of answer from the rest, and the lowercase 'i'd' looks sloppy.
screens.why5: Fresco and how it works are on the idea card on purpose, and nothing here sounds like company talk or a label for people like me.
screens.why6: It says fine and I can hold four options, but 'Only if I'd seen it work on one walk first' is a mouthful among one- and two-word answers.
screens.instead: To use Fresco, you'd take short videos and talk over them on your walks. Would you do that, or not? Yes; Only after seeing it work once; or No. Or say I can't tell.
